name: Vonage
one_liner: Communications API platform (SMS, Voice, Messages, Verify, Video, Identity/Network APIs).
auth_notes: Account API key + secret (Basic or request params) for Numbers, Account, SMS, Verify v1 etc.; Application JWT (RS256 signed with app private key) for Voice, Messages, Verify v2, Video; signed SMS via signature secret; webhooks verified via HS256 JWT. OAuth 2.0/CIBA only for Network APIs and the separate Business Communications line.
access_notes: Sign up at dashboard.vonage.com to get API key and secret immediately; free credit on signup, then pay-per-request. US A2P SMS needs 10DLC registration.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve signup gives key/secret and JWT-app auth; broad documented REST API with webhooks and official SDKs. Pay-as-you-go cost and 10DLC/regulatory registration are operational caveats, not credential gates.

needs_human_reason: Confirm product line wanted (core Communications APIs vs Business Communications); endpoint count and rate limits not verified.

evidence.quote: To work with our APIs, you will need to sign up for an account. This will give you an API key and secret
When you create a Vonage account, an API key and secret will be created for you.
US A2P SMS requires 10 DLC registration before sending application-to-person messages to US numbers.
The Vonage MCP Server enables AI agents and developer tools to discover, describe, and use Vonage capabilities via the Model Context Protocol.

disputes.why: Core APIs use API key/secret Basic and RS256 application JWT; OAuth is only for Network/Business Comms.
Dashboard signup yields key/secret instantly with free credit; no approval gate for core APIs.
Self-serve credentials, documented broad API, standard auth; UNCLEAR is not in rubric.
Vonage Communications APIs is the clear product; Business Communications is a separate line.
Auth table lists ~25 distinct APIs (SMS, Voice, Messages, Verify, Video, Numbers...), implying well over 100 endpoints.
Official MCP server overview exists on vendor docs domain.
